commit.subject: fix(tui): align grapheme widths with terminal cells (#6987)
commit.body_excerpt:
Intl.Segmenter can group Indic conjuncts and spacing marks into one grapheme even when wcwidth-style terminals allocate multiple cells. Count visible consonants after marks and Unicode spacing marks separately while preserving zero-width exceptions.

This is a compatibility heuristic. Unicode Spacing_Mark indicates positive advance, not a full terminal cell; Kitty keeps many Indic continuations in the initial cell, while xterm-style terminals advance for them, so Pi overcounts some clusters in Kitty.

Overcounting causes horizontal drift, but undercounting can trigger terminal autowrap, so this change favors overcounting.

Clusters can contain repeated marks and mark-consonant continuations, so this implementation leaves their widths uncapped. Collapsing them would undercount terminals that advance for every visible continuation.

Mode 2027 does not report cluster widths, so Pi still needs local width calculations. This change does not implement OSC 66, which would be preferable where supported.

Fixes #6124

Co-authored-by: Mario Zechner <badlogicgames@gmail.com>

commit.subject: fix(tui): restrict fast-echo bypass to ASCII so Vietnamese/CJK/IME input renders correctly (#26011)
commit.body_excerpt:
* fix(tui): restrict fast-echo bypass to ASCII so Vietnamese/CJK/IME input renders correctly

The composer's fast-echo path (canFastAppend / canFastBackspace) writes
characters straight to stdout to skip an Ink re-render on the hot
typing path. The previous guard only checked
'stringWidth(text) === text.length', which lets a lot of non-ASCII
through:

  - Vietnamese precomposed letters (ề, ắ, ờ, ự, ...) report width 1 and
    length 1, but a Vietnamese Telex / IME stack produces them across
    multiple keystrokes; the intermediate composition state must be
    drawn by Ink so the rendered cell, the stored value, and the
    cursor column stay in lockstep when the final commit replaces the
    preview.
  - NFD combining marks (U+0300..U+036F) are zero-width but length 1,
    so even a passing equality lets them slip and silently desync the
    cell column.
  - CJK/East-Asian wide and emoji rejected only because their length
    differs, but the boundary was shape-shaped, not intent-shaped.

User-visible bug from the original report:
  Example: eê noiói nge neène
  -> the bypass committed the IME preview char before the diacritic
     replaced it, leaving doubled letters on screen.

episode.after: At 9fb40e6a3d6338b6a6a616010de7a16672148924, direct append and backspace are permitted only when the affected text is nonempty printable ASCII and the existing end-of-line, single-line, non-wrapping, focused-TTY conditions also hold. Non-ASCII, combining, wide, emoji, control, multiline, middle-edit, and wrap-boundary cases fall through to normal rendering. Exported pure eligibility helpers make this boundary directly testable.
episode.diff: The change adds a printable-ASCII predicate and two pure fast-path eligibility helpers, replaces the prior display-width equality checks at both stdout bypass call sites with those helpers, preserves the existing direct stdout writes and deferred synchronization for eligible ASCII edits, and adds a focused 19-test regression matrix covering accepted ASCII plus rejected Vietnamese, combining-mark, CJK, emoji, control, NBSP/Latin-1, cursor-position, multiline, empty-input, and wrapping cases.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 9fb40e6a is the implementation-bearing resolution for issue/PR 26011, with parent d5416284, and changes only the text-input implementation and a new focused test file.

The parent implementation admitted append text when stringWidth(text) equaled text.length and admitted backspace when the removed grapheme's stringWidth was one, in addition to the common fast-echo base and line-shape conditions.
Before the change, successful append and backspace eligibility caused direct stdout writes and commits that skipped immediate local and parent synchronization.
The new append eligibility helper requires the cursor at the end, a nonempty single-line value, printable ASCII inserted text, and a resulting line width strictly below the terminal column count.
The new backspace eligibility helper requires deletion at the end of a nonempty single-line value and admits the removed grapheme only when it consists entirely of printable ASCII.
The component combines the existing focused, unmasked, unselected TTY precondition with the new pure helpers before selecting the direct append or backspace paths.
Eligible ASCII edits retain the optimized direct stdout behavior, while failed eligibility falls through to the ordinary edit and render flow.
Append tests preserve the intended ASCII fast path and reject unsafe structural states: cursor not at end, empty placeholder state, multiline input, and an append reaching the wrap column.
Append regression tests reject precomposed Vietnamese letters, Vietnamese tone-mark letters, NFD combining marks, CJK, emoji, ANSI/control text, NBSP, and Latin-1 letters.
Backspace tests preserve deletion of a final ASCII character and reject middle-of-line or empty deletion, multiline values, Vietnamese, CJK, NFD-composed graphemes, and emoji.
The patch extracts pure eligibility helpers, replaces the two width-based guards, and adds the dedicated fast-echo regression suite without redesigning the normal renderer.

The commit message reports that the regression matrix was red under the previous guard for 11 of 20 checked cases and green under the new guard; this is author-reported validation rather than a test execution performed during extraction.

The implementation explains that display-width equality is insufficient because a precomposed Vietnamese character can have both length one and width one while still participating in multi-keystroke IME composition.

title: Replace unstable emoji-width markers in terminal-visible text
before: At parent 52f875a875c20e927092a8b3aeb162614797543a, terminal-visible statuses, notices, summaries, and labels used emoji or emoji-presentation sequences such as 🟢, 🟡, 🔴, 🔄, ⏳, 🔎, 🚫, 💡, ✅, ❌, 🔒, and ⚠️. These strings could occupy two terminal columns or vary by renderer. Several state indicators also depended on color, and translated message keys and documentation embedded the old markers.
after: At a756676b2180bd5ba8c0062f98f140c5f0a9e732, affected strings use narrower text-presentation symbols such as ✓, ✗, ◐, ●, ◌, ◎, ★, ▸, ▷, and ⚠, or omit redundant decorative prefixes. Connected, connecting, and disconnected IDE states have distinct text shapes independent of color. Locale keys and selected documentation are reconciled with the changed strings, while tests and snapshots assert representative rendered output and explicitly drive MCP connection states.
diff: The implementation-bearing commit modifies 39 files with 251 insertions and 241 deletions. It replaces or removes emoji markers across CLI rendering, emitted session messages, and formatted agent statistics; strips U+FE0F from warning/info sequences; updates nine locale files and two user documents; revises unit assertions and Ink snapshots; and repairs MCP status tests so connecting and disconnected branches are selected through the component's serverStatus input instead of an ineffective module spy. The diff also changes some non-TUI strings, including retry-loop directives and PR attribution, so the change is broader than a purely terminal-rendering patch.

episode.before: At parent 52f875a875c20e927092a8b3aeb162614797543a, terminal-visible statuses, notices, summaries, and labels used emoji or emoji-presentation sequences such as 🟢, 🟡, 🔴, 🔄, ⏳, 🔎, 🚫, 💡, ✅, ❌, 🔒, and ⚠️. episode.after: At a756676b2180bd5ba8c0062f98f140c5f0a9e732, affected strings use narrower text-presentation symbols such as ✓, ✗, ◐, ●, ◌, ◎, ★, ▸, ▷, and ⚠, or omit redundant decorative prefixes. Connected, connecting, and disconnected IDE states have distinct text shapes independent of color. Locale keys and selected documentation are reconciled with the changed strings, while tests and snapshots assert representative rendered output and explicitly drive MCP connection states.
episode.diff: The implementation-bearing commit modifies 39 files with 251 insertions and 241 deletions. It replaces or removes emoji markers across CLI rendering, emitted session messages, and formatted agent statistics; strips U+FE0F from warning/info sequences; updates nine locale files and two user documents; revises unit assertions and Ink snapshots; and repairs MCP status tests so connecting and disconnected branches are selected through the component's serverStatus input instead of an ineffective module spy. candidate_workflows.title: Replace lossy table truncation with Unicode-aware wrapping
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for terminal tables that lose long content or mismeasure emoji and East Asian text: establish a display-cell width contract, allocate columns within structural overhead, normalize renderer-owned header markup, wrap content, render aligned continuation rows, and verify representative snapshots.

workflow_graph.goal: Preserve complete markdown-table content in a bounded terminal while maintaining display-cell-correct columns and borders for ASCII, emoji, and East Asian scripts.
when_to_use: A terminal table truncates long headers or cells even though vertical wrapping is acceptable.
Column widths or padding are computed from code-unit or plain string length and become unreliable for emoji or wide scripts.
The renderer receives an explicit terminal-width budget and owns table borders, padding, and row layout.
anti_goals: Do not change the semantic contents of table cells merely to make them fit.
Do not optimize for a fixed character count when terminal display width is the relevant invariant.
Do not remove inline rendering or renderer-owned header styling.
Do not introduce horizontal scrolling or widen the terminal as a substitute for bounded wrapping.
not_applicable_when: The output surface does not have terminal display-cell width semantics.
The product explicitly requires ellipsis truncation or a single-line row contract.
No terminal-width budget or equivalent layout constraint is available.
The text system cannot preserve styling through measurement and wrapping and no compatible styled-character adapter exists.

header styling ownership rules
representative ASCII and Unicode rendering cases
